key_insight: Human experts and LLMs performed similarly in generating viable materials synthesis recipes, and their closed-loop collaboration helped discover a new material prototype.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that combining human judgment with LLM-generated synthesis plans can accelerate experimental materials discovery, especially in underexplored compositional spaces.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper candidates using both humans and LLMs.
Tested recipes in the lab and fed results back into a closed-loop collaboration process.
Compared success rates across two rounds to assess learning and discovery performance.
evidence_signal: In-lab evaluation showed comparable success rates for humans and LLMs on known materials and much lower rates on unknown materials, with a new compound, Ba3PtO5, discovered.
watch_item: Results are limited by the specific Ruddlesden-Popper phase space and may not directly generalize to other materials families or synthesis constraints.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
